title: Exclusive Fullscreen on Windows causes critical VRAM memory leak (OpenGL and Vulkan)
body: ### Tested versions 4.5.1-stable ### System information Going off several user reports that shared their system info: 1) AMD 5600x, RTX 2070, 32gb DDR4 3600 MH 2) Operating System: Windows 11 Pro (Version 10.0.26200, Build 26200) System Manufacturer: ASUS x64-based PC CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D — 8 Cores / 16 Threads @ 4.7 GHz Motherboard: ASUS ROG STRIX X870E-H GAMING WIFI7 Revision: Rev 1.xx BIOS: American Megatrends Inc. 0209 (10.06.2025) BIOS Mode: UEFI RAM: 32.0 GB GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Adapter Type: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (NVIDIA compatible) VRAM: 1,048,576 Bytes reported (value truncated by Windows report — actual VRAM not properly enumerated) Driver Version: 32.0.15.7688 Driver Date: 07.03.2025 Driver Provider: NVIDIA Resolution: 1920 × 1080 @ 60 Hz For more information see: https://steamcommunity.com/app/3618390/discussions/0/687494691491497890/ ### Issue description I'm the developer of Gamblers Table and we just released, but out of nowhere tons of bug reports and negative reviews complaining about sudden crashes came flooding in. Apparently the RAM went OOM and crashed. Thanks to a volunteer that shared their screen I was able to watch their task manager. Everytime their triggered an ingame event that plays an AnimationPlayer (with CPUParticle2D) the VRAM memory spiked. Here is the screenshot of the taskmanager as they repeatedly trigger the event. It is extremely important to note that this **only happens in exclusive fullscreen**. And apparently only on Windows 11. After the VRAM runs full, it then goes over into the the shared memory where it ends up causing the RAM to go OOM. The user reporeted that this happens even without using this event and just after some time (20 to 30 minutes), but I'm not entirely sure if this is true as I was not able to confirm that behaviour in his screen sharing. I then asked the user (before their system crashes) whether they could go into window mode and then this happened: All the previously occupied memory has been immediately freed! The "fix" ended up changing from exclusive mode to normal fullscreen mode. ```swift // before (causes VRAM leak) DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN if toggled_on else DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MAXIMIZED) //after (does not cause leak) DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN if toggled_on else DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_MAXIMIZED) ``` Before the fix, users have reported that they tried both Vulkan and OpenGL, but it still crashed for them. All reports said they were using Windows 11. Here are further screenshot and logs they shared: Windows Event Log: ``` Faulting application name: gamblers-table.exe, version: 1.1.3.0, time stamp: 0x6930a7e4 Faulting module name: nvoglv64.dll, version: 32.0.15.7688, time stamp: 0x685b02b0 Exception code: 0xc0000005 Fault offset: 0x0000000000e6cf81 Faulting process id: 0x6638 Faulting application start time: 0x1DC83F2B517D116 Faulting application path: X:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Gamblers Table\gamblers-table.exe Faulting module path: C:\WINDOWS\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\nvmd.inf_amd64_949b704772ff9f4b\nvoglv64.dll Report Id: 0fc8074b-eba7-41a9-be37-f310a6127458 Faulting package full name: Faulting package-relative application ID: ``` (Tho this OpenGL error output still happens despite being in windowed mode and also after the fix. So this may be unrelated, but also only on Windows, not on Linux) ### Steps to reproduce I'm sorry to say that I don't have a reproducible build yet as I don't use Windows at all and I can't debug it. I thought it important to at least have an open issue for this already, as it seems extremely critical. Please see this steam discussion for more information about the user systems: https://steamcommunity.com/app/3618390/discussions/0/687494691491497890/ ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) As above, I can not reproduce it myself at this moment as I am on linux only and I can only go by user reports. Linux does not seem affected by this.
